text:
Take the neutrino as effectively massless and use \(c=1\). Since the pion is initially stationary, the muon and neutrino have equal and opposite momenta \(p\).

Energy conservation gives
\[
m_\pi=E_\mu+E_\nu,
\qquad E_\nu=p,
\qquad E_\mu^2=p^2+m_\mu^2.
\]

Thus
\[
E_\nu=p=\frac{m_\pi^2-m_\mu^2}{2m_\pi}
=\frac{139.6^2-105.7^2}{2(139.6)}
\approx 29.8\ \text{MeV}.
\]

The muon’s kinetic energy is
\[
K_\mu=m_\pi-m_\mu-E_\nu
=139.6-105.7-29.8
\approx 4.12\ \text{MeV}.
\]

Therefore, the kinetic energies of \(\mu^+\) and \(\nu\) are \(4.12\ \text{MeV}\) and \(29.8\ \text{MeV}\), respectively.

Answer: A
